  - resources/23-sql-best-practices-olap.md §3.1G — Added ONE new paragraph ('Honest fallbacks when there is NO unique column.') immediately AFTER the iter568 'Tie-break determinism.' paragraph (line ~592) and BEFORE the DO NOT WRITE blockquote (line ~594). Verbatim added: '**Honest fallbacks when there is NO unique column.** Sometimes the table genuinely has no second-column unique key to break ties on. **DO NOT** try `ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY user_id ORDER BY ts DESC, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (...))` — a nested window function inside another window function's `ORDER BY` is **REJECTED by the Trino 467 analyzer** (`StatementAnalyzer.analyzeWindowFunctions` raises an error; see [trinodb/trino PR #23929](https://github.com/trinodb/trino/pull/23929) and [Issue #24163](https://github.com/trinodb/trino/issues/24163)) AND it's semantically circular — the inner `ROW_NUMBER` adds no real distinguishing key, it just renumbers the same tied rows. Use one of these instead: **(a) Add EVERY remaining column to the ORDER BY as a deterministic-given-values tiebreaker** — `ORDER BY ts DESC, col_a, col_b, col_c` — deterministic across runs as long as no two rows are byte-identical (if they are, the rows are duplicates and no tiebreaker can distinguish them — they belong dedup\'d). **(b) Add a SURROGATE sequence column at INGEST time** — a monotonic `_ingest_seq BIGINT` / generated id assigned by the Spark ingest job (e.g. via `monotonically_increasing_id()` or a UUID column written into the Iceberg table). This is the robust real-world fix: solve the missing-unique-key problem at the source. **(c) When you genuinely don\'t care WHICH tied row wins**, drop `ROW_NUMBER() = 1` entirely and use the deterministic-by-`ts` representative-value form from [§3.1D]: `max_by(payload, ts)` (or `arbitrary(payload)` if you don\'t even care about latest-by-ts). `max_by` returns the `x` associated with the maximum `y`; `arbitrary` returns any non-null value.' Placed at the canonical §3.1G LEADING CANONICAL block (highest findability — matches Q2 tie-break / no-unique-key phrasing).

WebSearch verification (verbatim quotes):
  - PR #23929 (https://github.com/trinodb/trino/pull/23929 — 'Support ORDER BY in window functions'): 'In StatementAnalyzer.analyzeWindowFunctions, there is a need to explicitly check that there are no nested windows in the ORDER BY clause, with the check currently done only for the aggregation arguments. The key problem identified in the PR is that queries like `select array_agg(a ORDER BY last_value(b) OVER()) OVER (partition by c)` succeed by silently ignoring the inner window. The check needs to be generalized to work for ORDER BY and FILTER in addition to aggregation arguments.'
  - Issue #24163 (https://github.com/trinodb/trino/issues/24163 — 'Window ordering is not enforced for `ntile` and ranking window functions'): companion issue to PR #23929 covering ranking/ntile ORDER BY enforcement per ISO/IEC 9075-2:2023(E).
  - `arbitrary(x)` / `max_by(x, y)` valid Trino 467 — verified via Trino aggregate functions doc (trino.io/docs/current/functions/aggregate.html): '`max_by()` function returns the value of x associated with the maximum value of y over all input values' and '`arbitrary()` returns an arbitrary non-null value of x, if one exists' — aggregate signatures stable across versions 389/399/407/427/467/478/480/481. Both already used as Trino 467 canonical in resources/23 §3.1D since iter500-range; this iter569 paragraph reuses the existing canonical form, no new function call introduced.
  - `ROW(...)` constructor / ROW type valid Trino 467 — verified at trino.io/docs/current/language/types.html: 'A structure made up of fields that allows mixed types. The fields may be of any SQL type.' Example: `CAST(ROW(1, 2e0) AS ROW(x BIGINT, y DOUBLE))`.
